subtype: Approach: ending it kindly after honest reflection [Revision]
passage: Kunal, you asked me how I knew it was time, so let old Kashish tell you. Rohan and I, we were together in college and then apart in different cities for a year. We talked, properly, more than once. I wanted to start a business at home. Rohan wanted a research career abroad. Each time we found a way to say "we can manage", and each time it felt more like a sentence to repeat than a promise. One evening I said, "I think the distance isn't working, and I think it's because we want different lives." Rohan was quiet, then said, "I've been thinking the same." We cried a little. We agreed to be kind, to say a proper goodbye, and to write in a year. It hurt. It was also clean.

qa.q: How long had Kashish and Rohan been in different cities?
qa.a: They had been in different cities for a year.

qa.q: What was Kashish feeling when saying the words about the distance?
qa.a: Kashish was sad and unsure but honest, since the words came after many talks and ended in a little crying.

qa.q: What choice inside the story kept the parting respectful, and why?
qa.a: Kashish said the truth plainly and asked to be kind and say goodbye properly, because a clear honest ending left less room for blame.

qa.q: How might Rohan have felt on hearing it?
qa.a: Rohan was quiet, then said the same thing had been on Rohan's mind, which suggests relief mixed with sadness that Kashish spoke first.

grounding: Shows ending a long-distance relationship kindly after repeated honest conversations about different goals.
